rulings.raw: 1 pound turkey sausage (sweet or spicy with casings removed (I used spicy))
rulings.evidence: Fresh raw turkey sausage in casings: not smoked-turkey-sausage or kielbasa (smoked is a different product and price) and not italian-sausage, which is pork. I kept the 2026-08-26 ruling's id rather than mint a near-duplicate; sweet and hot are flavour variants of one tray SKU.
No commodity claims it, captures carry it. Asiago is an aged specialty wedge priced well above mozzarella or provolone, so no bridge to those ids; new id proposed.
REUSE of the live hamburger-buns id (6 of 7, cheapest 0.1658 at Fareway); whole wheat is a variety of the same 8-pack bun SKU on the same shelf, not a form flip in weight or price class.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Searched the board for turkey sausage under other spellings: smoked-turkey-sausage is the smoked rope (different product, different price), kielbasa is pork smoked sausage, italian-sausage is pork. Nothing prices fresh raw turkey sausage. The id name carries 'sweet' but the line allows sweet or spicy - the same tray SKU family - so alias rather than mint a second id if a spicy variant appears.

Not priced under another name: parmesan is a different aged cheese and price, mozzarella-cheese and provolone-cheese are fresh/semi-soft at half the per-oz price, and the bagged shredded-cheese id is cheddar/blend. Captures carry Asiago wedges today, so a null would pantry-price half a pound of specialty cheese.
